We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

title: Corrugated Niobene: Stability, Mechanical and Electronic Properties from First-Principles Calculations
abstract: The growing diversity of two-dimensional (2D) materials has expanded opportunities in electronics, energy technologies, catalysis, and optical applications. Within this landscape, understanding how corrugated architectures accommodate metallic bonding and influence the stability and properties of monoelemental niobium sheets remains an open research direction. Here, we propose a corrugated niobene nanosheet, denoted c-Nb, and investigate its structural, energetic, vibrational, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties using density functional theory simulations. The optimized structure adopts a centrosymmetric P-3m1 symmetry, with six atoms per primitive cell and a geometrical thickness of 4.279 Angstrom. Its cohesive energy of -6.03 eV/atom indicates strong binding relative to isolated atoms, although bulk BCC Nb remains energetically favored by 2.49 eV/atom. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies along the investigated high-symmetry path and the positive-definite in-plane stiffness matrix support dynamical and mechanical structural stability. Despite its pronounced corrugation, the nanosheet exhibits isotropic in-plane elasticity, with Young's and shear moduli of 43.66 N/m and 13.66 N/m, respectively, and a Poisson's ratio of 0.598. Electronic states near the Fermi level are dominated by Nb 4d orbitals, establishing multiband metallicity. These findings identify a corrugated structural candidate that combines strong cohesion, elastic compliance, and metallic electronic behavior, extending the structural diversity of monoelemental 2D metals and providing a basis for further exploration of niobium nanosheets in electronic and ultraviolet-responsive systems.

title: Redox-Programmed Bipolar Membranes from Electronically Wired Ion-Insertion Hosts for Selective Ion Transport
abstract: Selective ion separation is critical for resource recovery, water purification, and electrochemical energy technologies, yet it remains difficult to combine high selectivity, high flux, and simultaneous transmembrane uptake and release in a single-membrane architecture. Conventional polymer membranes are scalable but often lack molecular specificity. Redox-active ion-insertion materials provide lattice- and redox-defined ion selectivity, but their transport requires electronic charge compensation, limiting their use as single-stage transport membranes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Predictive Synthesis of MOFs and COFs
abstract: Predictive synthesis concerns the prospective modeling of how a targeted structure can be realized. The synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) intrinsically involves a multidimensional space of interdependent variables, posing a challenge for bench chemists to parameterize and predict. In this Perspective, we discuss the evolution from chemical-intuition-driven experimentation toward the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in the laboratory. By virtue of prior knowledge, uncertainty, and experimental failure in determining what should be attempted next, we envision predictive synthesis progressing from static recipe recommendation toward real-time control and transferable principles of framework formation. In this context, the significance lies in transforming trial-and-error practice into a means of measurable chemical reasoning, thereby accelerating crystalline materials discovery and advancing synthetic chemistry.

title: Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases for Amortized Conditional Interpretability
abstract: Gradient-based attribution provides input-specific information about model parameters, but computing it via backpropagation for many samples is expensive, while static importance scores discard input dependence. We derive KPSA (Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlas) from a block decomposition of the empirical neural tangent kernel. It measures normalized parameter-group sensitivity, embeds those sources in an explicit query space, and uses a lightweight kernel to estimate sensitivities for unseen inputs. We derive bounds that separate finite-source from irreducible representation error and give margin-based top-$k$ recovery. This paper studies two interpretability applications. Firstly, KPSA identifies parameter groups with high susceptibility to perturbations across vision, forecasting, and protein-modeling setups. Across a fivefold range of parameter budgets ($0.02$-$0.1\%$), its selected groups attain $39$-$85\%$ of the perturbation susceptibility of a first-order backpropagation oracle. In vision and forecasting, these parameter groups form sparse sensitivity circuits that extend across depth and vary systematically with the input. Secondly, we use KPSA on an activation-attribution problem for MLP features in transformers. It retains $81\%$ of the gap between a backpropagation oracle and a constant-sensitivity baseline on vision while increasing batched query-time throughput from 551 to 2,041 images/s and reducing peak GPU memory from 4.55 to 0.44GB. On the protein-modeling task, it recovers $68\%$ of this gap. An ablation of KPSA's kernel aggregation shows that nearest-neighbor retrieval in KPSA space can remain competitive. The empirics show that compact kernel atlases can store useful input-dependent parameter sensitivity while amortizing repeated gradient attribution, a step toward scalable conditional interpretability. Code can be found at https://github.com/Axym-Labs/kpsa .

title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

title: Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport
abstract: Aligning two independently pretrained unimodal encoders typically demands millions of paired examples. In this paper, we study the regime where only $N \sim 100$--$500$ pairs are available, while unpaired data on either side is abundant. Our method expresses every representation by its similarities to the $N$ paired anchors, which places both modalities in a common coordinate system; matches the two point clouds with a single entropic optimal transport problem solved over the entire pool, whose marginal constraints counteract the hubness that defeats nearest-neighbor matching; and distills the resulting plan into two lightweight encoders, so that the correspondence becomes inductive. We additionally put this marginal constraint in relation with the one-step hub corrections of the bilingual lexicon induction literature. Pairing is required only for the anchors: the unpaired collections may be drawn independently from the two marginals, so that no item outside the anchor set needs to have both of its modalities observed. We evaluate on image-text and molecule-text alignment, where our method outperforms existing approaches at the same anchor budget on Flickr30k, MS-COCO and ChEBI-20.

title: Drude, Where's My Charge? End-to-End Learning of Polarizable Drude Force Fields for Polymer Electrolytes
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations of solid polymer electrolytes require force fields that are fast enough to converge ion transport over hundreds of nanoseconds, yet accurately describe the ion-polymer interactions that govern it. Fixed-charge force fields meet the first requirement but neglect electronic polarization, an effect often approximated by scaling ionic charges using empirically chosen factors. Here we present AutoDrude, a differentiable framework that parametrizes polarizable Drude force fields directly from DFT energies, forces, and dipoles, with no empirical tuning and at only 1.20 times the cost of a fixed-charge simulation. For PEO-LiTFSI, the dipole-constrained (hard-constraint) AutoDrude model reproduces the experimental ionic conductivity as accurately as the best charge-scaled model (17% versus 16% mean absolute percentage error). We compare the polarizable forcefield to fixed charge ones models by fitting a fixed charge model. Unlike the charge-scaled models tested here, however, AutoDrude also reproduces the dilute-limit cation transference number, its increase with salt concentration, and the absence of Li-TFSI contact ion pairs at low concentration. A penalty-based (soft-constraint) variant yields a closer fit to the DFT reference yet underestimates the conductivity by up to an order of magnitude, demonstrating that closer agreement with DFT training data alone does not guarantee accurate ion transport. These results indicate that although charge scaling can reproduce ionic conductivity the explicit inclusion of polarization is necessary to capture the concentration dependence of cation transport in PEO-LiTFSI.

title: Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel. Then, via first-principles calculations, a screening of 90 two-dimensional ambidentate-ligand based square organometallic lattices leads to the identification of three altermagnetic materials, namely Fe(taz)2Cl2 (taz = 1,2,4- triazine), Co(app)2Cl2, and Fe(app)2Cl2 (app = 1,4-azaphosphinine), all of which possess 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in valence bands, as well as notable piezomagnetic behavior. This study paves the way for achieving direction-dependent fully spin-polarization in altermagnetic materials.

title: Interpretable structure–spectrum mapping via manifold learning in amorphous In–Ga–Zn oxide
Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
abstract: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.

title: Theory of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling in a Fabry-Pérot Cavity
abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--Pérot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.

title: Ultrafast Aqueous Photoinduced Electron/Energy Transfer Reversible Addition–Fragmentation Chain Transfer Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly: Wavelength-Dependent Morphologies and Scalable Nanoparticle Preparation
abstract: Photoinduced electron/energy transfer–reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (PET-RAFT) polymerization offers a powerful route to oxygen-tolerant polymer synthesis under visible light, yet slow polymerization rates remain a persistent bottleneck for further development. Here, we report an aryloxy xanthate chain transfer agent (CTA) bearing a 2-naphthyloxy Z group that unlocks ultrafast aqueous PET-RAFT polymerization under orange light irradiation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.

title: Peritumoral ultrasound-driven multimodal AI model for predicting lymphovascular space invasion and prognosis in cervical cancer
abstract: PurposeAccurate preoperative assessment of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in cervical cancer (CC) remains challenging despite its importance for treatment planning and risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid model integrating peritumoral ultrasound radiomics features, deep learning features, and clinical data for preoperative prediction of LVSI in CC.

title: Unlocking High-Energy Sodium-Ion Batteries via Chemically Engineered Closed Pores in Hard Carbon
abstract: The low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) and limited plateau capacity hinder the enhancement of the energy density for hard carbon anodes. To address the above critical issue, this review focuses on chemically mediated engineering strategies for closed-pore construction to promote electrochemical performance through microstructure customization of hard carbon at the molecular scale. Specifically, a clear structure-property relationship linking microstructure to macroscopic electrochemical behavior is established.

title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization
abstract: Black-box optimization (BBO) arises in many scientific and engineering problems where objective evaluations are expensive and limited. Recent large language model (LLM) agents offer a new way to approach BBO by combining task semantics, computation, optimization tools, and feedback-driven decision making, showing great potential due to the integration with mathematically rigorous tools. However, existing agentic BBO studies use different task domains and system configurations, making their results difficult to compare and the effects of individual design choices hard to isolate. We therefore introduce AgenticBBO-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for agentic BBO spanning synthetic functions, hyperparameter optimization, database tuning, chip design, and molecular design under a unified finite-budget evaluation protocol. In our experiments, agentic BBO achieves higher family-averaged scores than direct LLM-based methods in all five domains and outperforms the best numerical optimizers in four. We further study three factors shaping agent performance: optimization tools, task information and prior knowledge, and the role of the LLM during search. Our results show that additional numerical tools do not consistently improve performance, task semantics are broadly useful while more specific priors are less reliable, and numerical optimizers can effectively absorb gains from search trajectories established by the agent. Finally, we introduce a five-task frontier challenge within AgenticBBO-Bench and evaluate seven LLMs under the Codex agent harness, where GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lie on the Pareto frontier of performance and cost among the evaluated models. Our code is available at https://github.com/lamda-bbo/agentic-bbo.

title: Direct Quantification of Molecular Helicity-Dependent Effective Magnetic Fields in Chiral Polypeptide/Ferromagnet Heterostructures
abstract: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) refers to structural chirality governing spin transport in chiral systems, with experimental signatures reported in both transport experiments and photoemission. Beyond influencing transport, recent experiments indicate that adsorbed chiral molecules can influence the magnetic state of adjacent ferromagnetic layers, suggesting the existence of chirality-induced effects whose origin and quantitative characterization remain lacking. Here, we investigate chirality-induced long-range magnetic interactions in a hybrid molecular/ferromagnetic multilayer beyond the conventional direct transport coupling. We demonstrate the long-range nature by decoupling the adsorbed chiral molecules from the magnet using an insulating spacer. We show that self-assembled monolayers of chiral polypeptides with a helical structure can act on a ferromagnetic multilayer via an enantiomer-dependent effective magnetic field that may be mediated by chiral phonons through the insulating layer. Using Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) microscopy with on-chip reference regions free of molecules, we directly quantify this field by measuring precisely the reproducible shifts of the local hysteresis loops. The extracted effective field reverses sign for opposite enantiomers and correlates with the enantiomeric excess. These results provide a direct and quantitative link between molecular chirality and magnetic response in hybrid heterostructures, establishing an experimentally accessible benchmark for a CISS-related effect.

title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming atomistic simulations by accessing unprecedented length and time scales. While pretrained equivariant graph neural networks achieve robust zero-shot performance for near-equilibrium properties across broad chemical spaces, their translation to complex materials dynamics remains fundamentally challenged by out-of-distribution reactive states, representation biases, and computational scaling limits. In this Review, we examine how physics-driven specialization extends the applicability of MLIPs to complex dynamical systems. We systematically evaluate the structural trade-offs in MLIP design: the undersampling of highly strained configurations, the prohibitive computational overhead of high-order message-passing architectures, and the necessity of nonlocal interactions for open and field-coupled systems. Through four demanding application contexts - electrified interfaces, compositionally fluctuating open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture - we establish a framework for observable-specific validation. Highlighting the complementary roles of universal foundation models and task-specific potentials, we emphasize that targeted adaptations must be rigorously benchmarked against intended observables. We conclude with a roadmap for developing physically consistent, hardware-aware force fields that seamlessly connect electronic-structure accuracy to macroscopic materials phenomena.

title: A Biomimetic Solvatochromic Chip With Optimized Chemical Diversity for On-Site Liquid Identification
abstract: Colorimetric sensors for instant and on-the-spot identification of organic liquids have been actively developed across diverse fields such as chemical hazard inspection, manufacturing process monitoring, and beverage safety. Multi-target sensing scenarios often necessitate large-scale sensor arrays, which inevitably increase the fabrication complexity, complicate visual interpretation, and exacerbate data redundancy. Here, we present a biomimetic photonic-gustatory chip (BiPC) comprising a polyacrylate-based solvatochromic disk (PSD) array. The elastic photonic crystal PSDs generate distinct color patterns when swelled by organic solvents. To fully unlock the sensing potential, a Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) framework was developed to assess the overall swelling cross-reactivity toward target liquids, facilitating the design of a compact PSD array with HSP-guided chemical diversity and maximized inter-solvent response distinctiveness. Using intuitive pattern recognition, an HSP-optimized four-PSD array effectively differentiates solvent types and mixing ratios, homologues and isomers, as well as alcoholic beverages. Furthermore, we developed a smartphone application that integrated image capture with deep-learning-assisted cloud computing for on-site solvent identification, achieving high accuracy (97.1% across 80 liquid classes) within 30 s. The HSP framework is generalizable to the design of compact sensor arrays for various field-deployable liquid sensing scenarios.

title: A structure-preserving neural density functional for the ions of a polymer electrolyte
abstract: Predicting the structure and response of inhomogeneous polymer electrolytes requires a description of ion correlations that retains molecular-scale accuracy while remaining transferable across spatial scales and geometries. We develop a neural density functional for electrolytes that preserves spatial symmetries, thermodynamic integrability and the Noether identities, with perfect screening recovered in stable, noncritical bulk states. Its nonlinear density dependence captures the concentration-dependent correlations missed by a pair closure, including a crossover from enhanced to suppressed long-wavelength number fluctuations at strong coupling. The functional describes density profiles at an untrained salt concentration and predicts bulk structure factors and the long-wavelength number response. Trained solely on planar density and internal-force profiles from molecular dynamics, the functional predicts ionic structure in larger domains and in two-dimensional external fields. On the same ion data, it is more accurate than three other neural density-functional architectures and keeps its accuracy with a quarter of the training runs, where the errors of the best alternative grow by about two thirds. The spatial transferability provides a necessary foundation for connecting molecular correlations to continuum predictions at larger scales.

title: The AML-Associated A338V Mutation Rewires GPR183 Signaling through C-Terminal Ensemble Redistribution
abstract: G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) rely on dynamic conformational ensembles to coordinate G protein activation and recruitment of regulatory transducers such as GPCR kinases and β-arrestins. The oxysterol receptor GPR183 has been implicated in hematological malignancies, including acute myeloid leukemia (AML), where a rare A338V substitution occurs within its intrinsically disordered C-terminal tail. Here, we combined bioluminescence/fluorescence resonance energy transfer, bioluminescence- and fluorescence-based assays as well as migration experiments, with molecular dynamics simulations and allosteric communication networks to define the structural and functional consequences of this mutation. The A338V variant preserved agonist potency and largely maintained or even enhanced agonist-induced Gi protein activation, likely by inducing different receptor core conformations. On the other hand, it consistently impaired GRK2 and β-arrestin2 recruitment across multiple experimental configurations. Atomistic simulations supported these observations and further suggested that A338V reshapes the conformational ensemble of the C-terminal tail, altering its disorder, compaction, and membrane interactions. In particular, the mutation redistributes lipid interactions of phosphorylation-prone serine and threonine residues within the tail, suggesting disrupted spatial presentation of regulatory motifs required for productive GRK2 and β-arrestin coupling. Importantly, overexpression of GPR183 A338V in differentiated HL-60 cells led to a significant increase in migration of these cells toward the chemoattractant. Together, these results identify the intrinsically disordered C-terminal tail of GPR183 as a determinant of selective transducer coupling and show how a single naturally occurring mutation within a GPCR intrinsically disordered region can alter its conformational ensemble, selectively modulate intracellular protein coupling, and affect receptor-mediated cellular behavior.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Automatic Generation of Inorganic Solid-State Electrolytes via Unified Multi-Modal Network
abstract: Accurate prediction of ion transport properties remains a key bottleneck in computational discovery of solid-state electrolytes, particularly because experimentally measured ionic conductivities are sparse and strongly dependent on crystal structure. Here we introduce USMNet, a unified structure-aware multimodal neural network that combines crystal-structure representations, compositional features, and physically motivated descriptors to predict lithium-ion conductivity.

title: Adsorption and Separation of Dihydroxybenzenes by Colorimetric Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest Crystals
abstract: Hydrogen-bonded Organic Frameworks (HOFs) form a rapidly expanding alternative to Metal Organic Frameworks (MOFs). Among HOFs, the Molecular Adsorbing Host•Guest ( MAHG ) crystals introduced here combine cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) macrocycles and a tetraacid derivative of diphenyl-viologen (TETRAC). Despite their non-porous crystalline framework, MAHG crystals enable the diffusion of dihydroxybenzenes (DHB), which tend to localize in specific crystalline sites.

title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C).

title: Elucidation of the Hematite Direct Reduction Mechanism Using In Situ Spectroscopy
abstract: Research on alternative energy storage technologies continues, especially in the grid-scale long duration space where traditional battery technologies (including lithium-ion) suffer from either cost or safety concerns. Conversion anodes leveraging multi-valent iron promise high capacities, but key microscopic details of the mechanism for conversion are unknown.

title: YB_Mol Studio: an agent-integrated visual editing platform for molecular and materials design
abstract: Molecular and materials design requires researchers to inspect structures, edit molecular objects and connect each change to computation. Artificial intelligence (AI) agents add another operating mode: they need executable molecular operations, visible intermediate states and a way to continue from prior results. Here we present YB_Mol Studio, an agent-integrated visual editing platform for molecular and materials design. Its molecular design core, yb_mol, represents atoms, bonds, coordinates, structural hierarchy and periodic information in editable molecular objects.

title: Phytochemical Analysis and evaluation of the Antioxidant Activity of Cissus microdonta Planch.
abstract: Cissus microdonta Planch. is traditionally used to treat jaundice in Madagascar. This study aimed to investigate the phytochemical profile of Cissus microdonta stems and evaluate its antioxidant activity. Hexane (1.75%), ethyl acetate (3.74%), and ethanol (1.67%) extracts of the plant stems were obtained by maceration. Phytochemical screening was performed. The antioxidant activity of the plant was evaluated using the DPPH assay. Compounds from the active extracts were isolated using liquid chromatography on silica gel and identified via spectroscopic analysis.

title: Damage–repair kinetics and phase stiffness in a site-diluted XY model: implications for irradiated superconductors
abstract: Neutron damage lowers the transition temperature of REBCO conductors approximately linearly with displacement damage, and annealing recovers part of it, implicating phase stiffness. We model this competition as a two-dimensional XY lattice of the superconducting phase whose sites are damaged at a rate rising with local phase disorder and repaired stochastically, simulated by kinetic Monte Carlo. A mean-field reduction predicts bistability; the lattice shows no hysteresis or dependence on the initial state in the ranges tested (L ≤ 64) because the closure of the reduction fails.

title: Metal/Support Interfaces Overcome Reactivity Constraints of the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: Oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts are limited by precious metal costs and reactivity limitations by bond order conservation. We establish a conceptual framework to explain how low-dimensional Pt, Au, and Ag films on low-cost carbide/nitride supports transcend these limitations. Electronegativity differences between metal films and support terminations govern interfacial charge transfer, producing ligand effects that stabilize metal films, and raise the maximum of the ORR volcano plot.

title: From Bulk Hygroscopicity to Nanoscale Water Activity: Breakdown of Continuum Theories in Sub-4 nm Secondary Organic Aerosols
abstract: Interactions between water and organic molecules in sub-10 nm clusters surrounded by air play a key role in the chemistry and microphysics of secondary organic aerosol (SOA). However, water-organic interactions in such small clusters are difficult to probe experimentally and remain poorly constrained. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to examine morphology, molecular interactions, and water evaporation energetics of nanoclusters formed by nine representative SOA compounds across sizes and water contents.

title: Chemical Non-Innocence in Mn Porphyrin-Catalyzed Nitrene Transfer
abstract: Manganese porphyrins have been widely employed as catalysts for nitrogen-group transfer (NGT) and oxygen-atom transfer (OAT) reactions with olefins and C–H bonds. These transformations are typically proposed to proceed via high-valent manganese nitrenoid and oxo intermediates, respectively. While porphyrin redox non-innocence — in which electron transfer from the ligand to the metal delocalizes high-valent states across the metal and the ancillary ligand — is well established.

title: Adaptation of a retrosynthetic tool to project-specific chemistry: oligomer synthesis case study
abstract: Retrosynthetic planning for discrete oligomers presents challenges that differ from those encountered for conventional small molecules because their synthesis often relies on repeated transformations applied at multiple related sites within a multistep route. In conventional template-based search, each application of a single-center reaction rule is represented as an independent action, causing repeated chemistry to consume additional search depth and potentially generating order-equivalent trajectories.

title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
abstract: Fatty-acid protocells growing by outer-leaflet monomer uptake accumulate a transbilayer area imbalance that is relieved by budding once the reduced imbalance Δa exceeds a critical value, as described by area-difference elasticity (ADE). It is tempting to read modern tumour ectosome shedding as the same physics. We show that the naive transfer fails, and derive the version that does not. A protocell is osmotically relaxed; the plasma membrane of a cancer cell is under tension (σ ≈ 0.01–0.1 mN/m), which imposes an area cost absent from the protocell treatment.

title: Fundamental Limitations of Cu(II)-based Oxides for Photoelectrochemical Nitrogen Reduction
abstract: The photoelectrochemical (PEC) nitrogen reduction reaction (N 2 RR) offers a potentially sustainable route to ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis. However, reliable evaluation of PEC N 2 RR activity remains challenging due to contamination-induced false positives and competing reactions. Here, we comparatively investigate p -type CuBi 2 O 4 and the previously reported PEC N 2 RR-active photocathode CuO, using an ultra-clean, contamination-controlled measurement system.

title: Autonomous Robotic Workflow for Solution-Based Synthesis and High-Temperature Thermal Processing toward Self-Driving Laboratories
abstract: The growing need has pushed the development of autonomous laboratory automation for high-throughput materials research. Although self-driving laboratories (SDL) and automated liquid handling have advanced significantly, robotic material handling remains poorly integrated with high-temperature thermal processes. In this study, a solution-based synthesis autonomous robotic process was designed, developed, calibrated, and validated.

title: Reversible Ion Transport Through an Irreversibly Percolating Li 2 S Interphase at the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl Interface
abstract: Interfacial resistance growth between Li metal and sulfide solid electrolytes is a leading cause of failure in solid-state batteries, yet the atomic-scale processes that govern this growth under an electrochemical driving force are poorly resolved. Herein, we combine a fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potential with dynamically updated atomic charges to simulate the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface for nanoseconds under both field-free and electric-field-driven conditions.

title: TRMC and NEXAFS Reveal Fast Electron Transfer to Ce3+/Oxygen-Vacancy Traps in Non-Covalent CexOy/C3N4 Interface for Photocatalytic H2
abstract: Earth-abundant photocatalysts for solar H₂ struggle to absorb deep visible light and separate charges at the same time. Here we show that a small amount of reduced ceria on carbon nitride achieves both. Non covalent CexOy/C3N4 heterostructures with 4% and 7% cerium oxide were compared with CeO2 and C3N4 references for H₂ evolution at 410 and 465 nm. The key turns out to be not how much ceria is added, but in which state and how well it is spread.

title: High-Spin Diradical-Dominated Chemiluminescence
abstract: We report a quantum-chemical investigation into the chemiluminescence mechanism of cyclometalated Ir (III) Schiff base complexes, promising chemiluminophores for biological imaging. The reaction proceeds via ring-opening of a key oxaziridine intermediate to yield a singlet diradical, which undergoes rapid intersystem crossing (ISC) to its triplet counterpart, followed by deprotonation to generate the emissive triplet product.

title: A Response Surface Methodology Framework for Targeted MALDI‑TIMS Optimization and in‑Tissue Metabolite Resolution
abstract: Differentiating hexose‑phosphate isomers directly within tissue is essential for understanding glycolytic and pentose‑phosphate pathway activity, particularly in the kidney, where these metabolites play central roles in energy balance, redox regulation, and stress response. However, their high structural similarity and low endogenous abundance make on‑tissue discrimination analytically challenging.

title: Structuring High-Entropy Oxides at the Nanoscale: Ordered Mesoporous (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox Thin Films for High-Performance Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysis
abstract: The synthesis of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with nanoscale architectures is challenging, since both the peculiar crystalline structure with statistical element occupancy and the desired nanomorphology must be controlled. Here, ordered mesoporous (spinel) (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox HEO thin films were prepared via soft-templating and dip-coating under tailored synthesis conditions, and the influence of calcination temperature on their structural evolution and alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance was investigated.

title: VIBE-VIEW and QVF: portable visualization and checksummed archives for quantum chemistry
abstract: Quantum-chemistry results often span separate files for structures, orbitals, scalar fields, and spectra. We present VIBE-VIEW, a viewer for molecular and periodic calculations, and QVF (Quantum Visualization Format), its producer-neutral archive format. QVF combines visualization data with provenance, citations, and optional job specifications and run records in one ZIP file. A JSON manifest declares payload formats and SHA-256 checksums, with dtypes and shapes for numeric arrays. Consumers verify payload integrity before use and explicitly report unsupported extensions.

title: How does spatio-temporal optimisation affect the siting and operation of direct air capture systems?
abstract: The climate crisis is driving the urgent development of negative emission technologies, such as adsorption-based direct air capture (DAC). Although DAC holds promise, it remains costly and requires further technological innovation, design optimisation, and supply chain development to scale effectively and achieve meaningful climate impact. DAC performance is influenced by both local ambient (e.g., temperature, humidity) and energy conditions (e.g., upstream emissions, costs).

title: Solid-state NMR and first-principle calculations reveal the structure and dynamics of Li-N-H materials
abstract: Lithium-nitrogen-hydrogen (Li-N-H) materials are promising for hydrogen storage, solid-state batteries, and lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis, yet their local structures and proton dynamics remain poorly understood because of compositional disorder and limited sensitivity of conventional diffraction methods. Here, we combine multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H, 7Li, 14N, and 15N ssNMR) with first-principles calculations to resolve the atomic environments and dynamics of Li3N, LiNH2, and Li1+xNH2-x (.

title: Active synthesizability prediction for a virtual space of 395 million catalyst candidates with small data
abstract: N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) are well established as catalysts and ligands in many chemical transformations. Recently, interest has grown in pyridine[1,5]imidazolium salt pre-catalysts, stable precursors to NHCs, because they are relatively easy to synthesize and highly adaptable. This work introduces a data-driven workflow to identify which pyridine[1,5]imidazolium salts are readily synthetically accessible, starting from exploratory synthesis attempts for 127 compounds.

title: Thioiminium Salt Catalyzed Chemoselective Late Stage Halogenation Using N-Halosuccinimides
abstract: C−H halogenation plays a central role in drug discovery. It enables rapid molecular diversification and provides a direct means to tune the metabolic and biological properties of drug candidates. However, selective halogenation of less reactive arenes remains challenging, particularly when aromatic and benzylic C−H bonds coexist in the same molecule. Here, we introduce a thioiminium salt-based Lewisbase catalyst that activates readily available N-halosuccinimides for selective aromatic and benzylic halogenation with complementary control.

title: Fischer Indole Synthesis Inspired De Novo and Modular Assembly of Indolines
abstract: Herein, we report a modular and redox-neutral strategy for the de novo synthesis of structurally diverse indolines. While conventional approaches often rely on prefunctionalized arenes or require oxidative/reductive steps, our method enables direct annulation from ortho-unsubstituted anilines and vinyldiazos. The sequence comprises a rhodium-catalyzed α-selective N–H insertion of vinyldiazoacetates, followed by TFA-promoted aza-Claisen rearrangement and intramolecular aza-Michael addition. This one-pot sequential protocol exhibits broad substrate generality and has been extended to an asymmetric version and intramolecular variant, allowing the synthesis of challenging seven-membered ring-fused indolines. DFT studies support a concerted mechanism via a chairlike transition state. With its operational simplicity and structural versatility, this methodology provides an efficient route to access privileged indoline scaffolds for pharmaceutical and synthetic applications.

title: MAST: Motif-Augmented Diffusion with Search Tree for Spectroscopic Molecular Structure Elucidation
abstract: Elucidating molecular structures from spectra is a foundational problem in chemical and materials characterization, yet remains challenging due to spectral ambiguity and the vast molecular space. Although recent diffusion-based generators show strong promise for spectra-conditioned elucidation, existing methods struggle to learn robust spectra-structure relationships from limited paired data when relying solely on global spectral representation. Moreover, the repeated full sampling inference strategy incurs substantial computation overhead. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MAST}, a \textbf{M}otif-\textbf{A}ugmented diffusion framework with \textbf{S}earch \textbf{T}ree, for joint 2D-3D spectroscopic molecular structure elucidation. MAST introduces explicit, interpretable \emph{motif priors} as intermediate evidences throughout denoising, reducing conditional ambiguity and facilitating spectra-conditioned optimization. We further cast diffusion sampling as \emph{reward-guided tree search} to prioritize high-reward denoising trajectories, yielding a compact set of spectra-consistent candidates under limited budgets. On the QM9S multi-spectra benchmark, MAST achieves \textbf{94.89\%} exact recovery and improves 3D fidelity, while preserving high chemical validity and stability. Code is available at https://github.com/Jia040223/MAST.

title: Structure Tax: How Structured Output affects LLMs Performance
abstract: Deploying large language models in production often requires constraining outputs to structured formats such as JSON or XML, and prior work treats the resulting accuracy loss as an inherent `structure tax'. We re-examine this claim by evaluating a battery of models, datasets and schemas, measuring task accuracy, confidence calibration, and hidden-state geometry. The tax turns out to depend on schema design rather than on structure per se: reasoning-first field ordering matches or exceeds free-form accuracy, while answer-first ordering causes steep drops, particularly in smaller models. Format sensitivity scales inversely with a task's own structural constraints, and schemas that preserve reasoning order also improve calibration with CKA showing greater separability between correct and incorrect representations in middle transformer layers. Our findings indicate that properly designed structured formats can match or exceed free-form performance, reframing the critical question from `whether to structure' to `how to structure' for optimal reasoning preservation.

title: Emergent gold-induced interfacial magnetism in monolayer FePS$_3$
abstract: Owing to their atomically clean interfaces and extreme thinness, two-dimensional (2D) materials are ideal hosts for strong proximity effects, whereby contact with an adjacent material reshapes their ground state. Here, we demonstrate such an effect within a hybrid heterostructure, between the 2D antiferromagnet FePS$_3$ and an ultrathin gold film. Rather than a passive support, the latter profoundly changes the nature of the magnetism in the 2D magnet, inducing a sizeable interfacial moment. Large-area flakes from Au-assisted exfoliation, combined with element-selective X-ray absorption mapping, enable a layer-by-layer study from monolayer to bulk, benchmarked against an inert SiO$_2$ substrate reference. At 9 T and 5 K, the monolayer on gold shows a three-fold enhanced X-ray magnetic circular dichroism relative to SiO$_2$, with a $\sim$40% reduction of the orbital-to-spin moment ratio. Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering reveals a collapse of the crystal-field (d-d) excitations and a massive spectral-weight transfer to the charge-transfer region, unveiling the microscopic mechanism behind this change. Supported by atomic multiplet calculations, we identify interfacial charge transfer and Fe 3d-Au hybridization as the origin of these effects, which decay over the first three layers and vanish at the pentalayer, establishing layer number combined with substrate engineering as an atomically precise handle.

title: Symmetry-Dependent Polarity Reversal of Bulk Spin-Orbit Torque in Single-Layer MnCoGa
abstract: Controlling the magnitude and polarity of spin-orbit torque (SOT) is essential for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices. Here, we realize bulk spin-orbit torque (SOT) in a single-layer Mn1.6Co1.4Ga (MCG) Heusler alloy and achieve lattice strain-controlled reversal of SOT polarity. SOT-driven magnetization switching is achieved over a thickness range of 3-20 nm, with the switching polarity reversed between the strongly strained ultrathin regime and thicker films. First-principles calculations reveal a sizable intrinsic spin Hall conductivity (SHC) in MCG originating from its topological band structure, which is enhanced by the tetragonal distortion without changing sign. Together with the thickness-dependent structural evolution, we demonstrate that the reversal of SOT polarity does not originate from a sign change of the SHC, but rather from lattice distortion induced symmetry breaking that modifies the conversion of spin current into a net bulk SOT, thereby controlling its polarity. These results establish strain-controlled structural symmetry as an additional degree of freedom for tuning bulk SOT in magnetic single layers.

title: MPGE: A Multi-Perspective Graph Explainer for Molecular Classification Explanation
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) predict molecular properties from chemical graph data, but predictive accuracy does not explain how graph information supports an individual decision. A compact prediction-preserving rationale does not necessarily reveal which changes reverse the decision or which modifications the model tolerates. We propose the Multi-Perspective Graph Explainer (MPGE), unifying factual support, counterfactual sensitivity, and exemplar tolerance for a frozen classifier. The factual view, originally termed prototype (PT), seeks a compact retained edge set with the same label and required confidence. Counterfactual (CF) explanations seek bounded prediction-changing deletions; exemplar (EXE) explanations seek non-trivial bounded deletions that preserve the label and confidence. A shared constrained formulation connects prediction behavior, compactness, and edit cost, while separate objectives generate the three views. Our graph-classification extension of CF-GNNExplainer learns symmetric edge rankings and verifies discrete candidates, recording unsuccessful searches. A separate BBBP fragment backend returns RDKit-sanitized molecules. We evaluate the primary GCN implementation on MUTAG, Mutagenicity, AIDS, COX2_MD, and BBBP using semantic coverage, conditional quality, stability, and runtime. Successful factual masks retained 8.6%--15.5% of input edges on average across datasets; bounded counterfactual coverage was 4.8%--67.6%, and exemplar preservation coverage was 98.9%--100.0%. Exploratory controls reveal the influence of hard projection and retained node information. Quantitative comparisons and molecular visualizations characterize model support, sensitivity, and tolerance without treating them as validated chemical mechanisms.

title: REACT: Rolling Denoising and Dual Decoupling for Reactive Robot Control with VLA Models
abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models generate action chunks for temporally coherent robot motion, but chunked control creates a fundamental closed-loop trade-off: long chunks provide smooth execution, whereas frequent replanning improves reactivity at the cost of action discontinuities. We introduce REACT, a rolling-denoising framework that makes flow-based VLAs more reactive while preserving long-horizon context. Instead of regenerating entire action chunks from scratch, REACT maintains a persistent action buffer with staggered flow timesteps. At each control step, the full horizon is denoised using the latest observation, the cleanest action block is executed, partially refined future blocks are shifted forward, and fresh noise is appended to the tail. As a result, each executed action block is refined across multiple recent observations before deployment. To support real-time control, we further introduce dual decoupling, which separates sensing, VLM encoding, DiT denoising, and action execution, enabling high-frequency observation updates and action streaming under practical compute constraints. Across the RoboTwin 2.0 simulation benchmark and real-world tasks spanning bimanual manipulation and dynamic control on multiple robot platforms, REACT improves task success and reduces reaction latency while producing smoother trajectories than frequent-replanning and asynchronous baselines.

title: Observing Elusive Reaction Intermediates with Raman Spectroscopy via Melt-React-Trap
abstract: Understanding reaction pathways relies on detecting and characterizing reactive and short-lived intermediate species. Melt-React-Trap (MRT) is introduced as a technique to generate and identify such elusive species via Raman microscopy. This method combines the advantages of low-temperature spectroscopy, rendering convenient the measurement of unstable molecules, with localized heating to allow thermal reactions. Using this approach, reagents are sequentially frozen, mixed in a cryomill and held under cryogenic conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Programming N-linked glycan composition through de novo protein design
abstract: N-linked glycans are ubiquitous post-translational modifications that mediate diverse biological processes, including cell signaling and adhesion, molecular recognition, and host-pathogen interactions. Despite their importance, N-linked glycans have largely remained beyond the reach of biomolecular design due to a lack of methods capable of jointly modeling glycans and protein structure. Here, we develop a general all-atom computational pipeline for creating de novo glycoproteins in which the amino acid sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. The method uses three-dimensional protein structure to tune glycan accessibility to processing enzymes in the eukaryotic secretory pathway. Systematic increases in steric restriction progressively reduced processing, shifting glycans from heterogeneous complex-type structures toward increasingly underprocessed oligomannose-type species resembling those found on many viral glycoproteins. Despite this programmed restriction, the resulting oligomannose glycans remained accessible for biological recognition, inhibiting uropathogenic Escherichia coli adhesion to human bladder cells and binding mannose-binding lectin. These results establish steric control of N-glycan processing as a genetically encodable design principle and extend computational protein design to functional glycoproteins with programmed composition.

title: Green-function thimbles for internal conversion
abstract: Oscillatory real-time integrals and the complete quadratic transformation between electronic-state normal modes are persistent obstacles in molecular internal-conversion calculations. We develop a finite-temperature Tyablikov–Moskalenko Green-function formulation that retains unequal frequencies, equilibrium displacement, Duschinsky rotation, the anomalous squeezing block, and a general first-order Herzberg–Teller nonadiabatic operator.

title: StereoAtlas: A Large-Scale Dataset of Chiral Compounds with Distinct Bioactivities Curated from ChEMBL37
abstract: Stereoisomers share identical two-dimensional molecular topology and exhibit a Tanimoto similarity score of exactly 1.0 under standard fingerprint methods, rendering their bioactivity differences invisible to conventional data-driven or physics-based activity prediction approaches. Here, we present StereoAtlas, a dataset of 155,526 experimentally measured true isomer families derived from ChEMBL37, in which paired or families of stereoisomers exhibited pharmacological activity for the same biological target, in the same organism.

title: Quantifying the Rate Performance of 3D-Printed LFP Electrodes from Water-Based Inks
abstract: Additive manufacturing enables the fabrication of battery electrodes with controlled architectures that can mitigate transport limitations at high activematerial loadings. In this work, water-based lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, LFP) inks containing carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as binder were processed by doctor-blade coating (DB) and direct ink writing (DIW) to fabricate planar and 3D-structured electrodes.

title: Meropenem degradation does not necessarily eliminate antibacterial activity: responses of model and environmental bacterial isolates
abstract: Carbapenems can degrade rapidly in aquatic systems, and disappearance of the parent compound is often interpreted as loss of antibacterial activity. Here, we compared the antibacterial effects of intact meropenem with those of a meropenem mixture incubated for eight days in the presence of biofilm-covered moving-bed biofilm reactor carriers. During incubation, parent meropenem became undetectable, while several transformation products (TPs) retaining a closed β-lactam ring, a key structural feature for antibacterial activity, formed and persisted through the incubation period.

title: Chemputing the synthesis and optimisation of arene fluorination in an automated platform
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) relies on the rapid and efficient incorporation of fluorine-18 (18F) into molecular imaging agents, yet selecting appropriate radiofluorination conditions for new substrates remains ad hoc. Whilst decades of development have generated a wealth of experimentally validated reactions, this knowledge remains dispersed throughout literature and is difficult to exploit systematically for reaction planning.

title: Polymer Property Prediction via an Automated Molecular Dynamics Pipeline and Transfer Learning
abstract: For many existing and emerging applications, there is a great need to develop novel polymeric materials with highly tuned properties. In the quest to design materials from highly abundant natural resources or waste materials, there is a vast design space that has remained substantially unexplored. Machine learning approaches can help guide toward improved properties, but these approaches often suffer from a lack of high quality data, the acquisition of which can be tedious, time-consuming, and expensive.

title: Copper binding to glucagon and glucagon-like peptide 1: Relevance to diabetes
abstract: Glucagon (GCG) and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP1) are hormones involved in maintaining glucose homeostasis. Diabetic patients display a chronic dysfunction of these hormones along with an increase in copper levels in the bloodstream. Although GCG(1–29) and GLP1(1–37) harbour Cu2+-anchoring groups at their N-terminal regions, their metal-binding properties have not been assesed, nor their implications in metal homeostasis/hormone function.

title: Möbius Kekulene
abstract: Encoding prescribed topologies in rigid conjugated frameworks offers a route to tuning electronic properties but is constrained by severe geometric strain. We synthesized and isolated Möbius kekulene, a compact, all-benzenoid double-stranded counterpart of planar kekulene. Its synthesis was enabled by strain-trajectory programming, in which precursor connectivity is designed to control strain accumulation during cyclization.

title: Atomic memory in molecular charge evolution in deep inner-shell Auger cascades.
abstract: A single low-keV X-ray photon can strip a molecule of more than ten electrons. Deep inner-shell ionization of heavy atoms, including those incorporated into radiosensitizers in emerging cancer therapies, initiates an Auger cascade that rapidly builds up high charge and can drive extensive fragmentation. How this charge accumulates, not the total energy deposited alone, governs the molecular response to irradiation.

title: Exact orientational thermodynamics of multipole rank pairs: a two-valued low-temperature heat-capacity law, with new data for 28 rank pairs (L = 2-24) and 29 real molecule pairs
abstract: New results and new data reported in this work. This paper reports a primary data set and the law it yields, not a survey of the literature. (i) Orientational partition functions 𝑍(𝑦) and low-temperature interaction heat capacities 𝛾 = 𝐶𝑣/𝑘𝐵 are computed for 28 multipole rank pairs spanning 𝐿 = 𝑛 +𝑚 = 2 to 𝐿 = 24, each entry obtained by up to three mutually independent numerical routes — the large-𝑦 tail of the thermal coupling function, the exact fluctuation formula, and the sublevel-volume exponent — and each with the coupling-minimum structure measured independently of the…

title: Engineering Bacteria and Their Vesicles for Therapy: Integrating Native Functions, Genetic Control, and Chemical Biology
abstract: Bacteria possess native capabilities that are difficult to reproduce using conventional therapeutic platforms, including active motility, environmental adaptation, localized proliferation, metabolite production, immune stimulation, and interactions with host-associated microbial communities. However, bacterial therapeutics are frequently organized either by microbial species or by engineering technology, obscuring how chassis selection, functional modification, and clinical application should be coordinated.

title: Mapping Spatially Heterogeneous and History-Dependent Hydrogel Mechanics Using Fluid-Driven Cyclic Shear
abstract: Soft porous materials in biological environments, such as the extracellular matrix, are frequently subjected to dynamic stresses transmitted by fluid motion, yet their internal deformation fields and microstructural evolution under repeated loading remain elusive. Here, we impose oscillatory shear on agarose hydrogels without solid contact by embedding a millimeter-scale gel block in a microfluidic channel and applying oscillatory pressure-driven flow over its exposed surface.

title: From torrefaction to pyrolysis: Influence of bamboo biochar production route on biochar characteristics and the thermal and mechanical performance of polylactic acid biocomposites
abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing has accelerated the development of sustainable polymer composites reinforced with bio-based fillers such as biochar. This study investigates how the biochar carbonization route affects the thermal and mechanical properties of polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites. Bamboo-derived torrefied biomass (TBB) and pyrolyzed biochar (PBB) were incorporated into PLA at loadings of 1 wt.% and 2 wt.%.

title: Utilization of heuristic approaches and molecular modelling to visualise chemical reactivity in small student groups
abstract: According to current psychometric analyses, a vast majority of novices in universities mostly utilize algorithmic mental processes to solve given tasks and tests. Although algorithmic thinking is an essential part of brain functions, experts on didactics call for methods which also develop conceptual thinking in beginners. In this sense, heuristic molecular modelling plays an important role in chemistry education since it inherently employs several conceptual thinking principles.

title: Spin states, electronic structure and phonon properties of ZnxFe[Fe(CN)6] (x = 0 – 1) by hybrid density functional theory
abstract: Hexacyanoferrates (HCF) or Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) have emerged as potent ion insertion materials for battery electrodes. They are also among the very few hosts in which reversible insertion of multivalent ions such as Zn 2+ into the framework is experimentally established. Zinc-containing ZnFe[Fe(CN) 6 ] members of the iron hexacyanoferrate series are particularly interesting for the anode-free zinc cells where cathode can supply the entire zinc inventory. Yet essentially nothing is fundamentally known about them.

title: Large language models as collaborators in molecular thermodynamics: a case study of the LLM-assisted development of SAFT-VR IMP, an equation of state for polar fluids
abstract: Whether large language models (LLMs) can contribute to non-trivial science, beyond summarising literature and writing routine code, is an open question. We report a case study in which an LLM (Claude) was asked to formulate, implement, verify and parameterise a new equation of state of the statistical associating fluid theory (SAFT) family. The target was a SAFT-VR variant for polar and dipolar molecules in which the segments interact through the isotropic multipolar potential (IMP) of Müller and Gelb, expressed as a temperature-dependent sum of Sutherland terms and treated with the…

title: Tryptophan-induced nanometrization and hydrophobization of Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ oxyhydroxide green rust crystals enable their insertion into lipid particles
abstract: Compartmentalization and metabolic activity are recognized as intrinsic and essential to both extant life and the first protocells. Minerals found in early-Earth hydrothermal settings, such as the Fe 2+/3+ oxyhydroxide green rust (GR), are not only expected to have promoted the formation and assembly of amphiphiles into vesicles, but also to have acted as precursors of current membrane-embedded bioenergetic enzymes.

title: New approach for deciphering polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-based plastics’ diols: Application on PET daily-life packaging objects paving their chemical modifications
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a thermoplastic polyester synthetized from a terephthalic diacid and a diol which is generally ethylene glycol. Given PET prominence in food packaging industry, a detailed study of this polymer is of utmost importance. The identification of the initial diols constituting PET-based bottles and containers along with their structural modifications, due to recycling procedures and/or weathering, is still a challenging research subject.

title: Expanded ensemble predictions of solvent–water partition coefficients for drug-like molecules using OpenFF 2.0 and GAFF 2.1
abstract: How well do general-purpose molecular mechanics force fields predict solvent–water partition coefficients for drug-like molecules? To answer this question, we performed massively parallel expanded ensemble free energy calculations using distributed computing to evaluate two widely used force fields—GAFF 2.1 and OpenFF 2.0—across a diverse set of 70 molecules and solvents (chloroform, dodecane, octanol and toluene). We find both force fields have comparable accuracy, with predicted transfer free energies having mean unsigned errors (MUEs) below 2 kcal/mol in nearly all cases.

title: From Peroxides to Qubits: Using Glow-Stick Chemistry to Introduce Excited States, Conical Intersections, and Quantum Computing to Undergraduates
abstract: Glow sticks provide a familiar and visually striking entry point to chemiluminescence and excited-state chemistry. We present a self-contained computational teaching module that uses peroxide bond breaking to introduce multireference electronic structure, conical intersections, and quantum computing. In a Jupyter/Google Colab notebook, students first stretch the O–O bond of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and observe the emergence of biradical character.

title: Efficient Customizable Synthesis Planning with Graph Grammars, with an application to Elastase B inhibitor candidates
abstract: Computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) software allows experimentalists to streamline setups and reduce unsuccessful experiments. CASP has a long history, yet remains an active research area. Although various tools have been developed and published, few have remained publicly available and continue to be supported. Those available at no-cost typically operate on generalized global databases, ignoring domain-or laboratory-specific constraints. Here, we present LAGER, a graph-grammar-based retrosynthesis engine built on the Double Pushout (DPO) formalism of the MØD framework.

title: Kinetic Target-Guided Discovery of Selective Nanomolar Hydroxamic Acid–Based Inhibitors of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Elastase LasB
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is increasingly becoming a critical threat to human health. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is classified as a high-priority pathogen, and treating it with traditional antibiotics is increasingly challenging. In this work, we report on a non-traditional approach: targeting Elastase B, a major virulence factor that drives P. aeruginosa pathogenicity.

title: Chirality Relay via Non-stereogenic Carbocations: from Stereogenic Alcohol to Twisted Tricyclic Skeleton
abstract: Stereogenic carbon loses its stereochemistry when it is converted into planar carbocation. Retention of the chirality is difficult unless static reference chirality is introduced within reactant to change the reactions diastereoselective. Herein we report a rare reaction in which a stereogenic alcohol gives a chiral twisted tricyclic skeleton by acid-mediated dehydrative cyclization. The intermediates are carbocations without any stereogenic centers, and their non-stereogenic conformational features relay the chiral information to the product.

title: From Industrial lignin biomass waste to bio-based organic semiconductors for sustainable electronics: a proof of concept based on Vanillin
abstract: Developing sustainable, bio-based organic semiconductors from renewable aromatic feedstocks opens new possibilities for sustainable electronics. Here, the present work uses vanillin as a sustainable aromatic platform extracted from industrial lignin biomass waste, which is chemically transformed into a π-conjugated semiconductor. The resulting donor–acceptor–donor molecule, IsoInd-CO-diCzBu, combines reversible redox activity with high thermal stability.

title: Combined Enhanced Conformational Sampling and Protein-Ligand Dockings on CYP3A4 Improves in Silico Prediction of Drug Metabolism
abstract: Cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) is the primary drug-metabolizing enzyme in humans. This is largely due to its highly flexible structure, which enables it to bind a broad spectrum of xenobiotics with a wide variety of shapes and physicochemical properties. This plasticity, however, presents challenges for in silico substrate prediction methods, in particular those that consider only a limited conformational space of the receptor or that rely on static crystal structures.

title: Beyond special quasirandom structures: free energies from energy cumulants
abstract: Predicting the finite-temperature stability of a disordered phase requires its free energy. It is traditionally approximated by combining the energy of a special quasirandom structure (a small cell mimicking a random alloy) with the ideal configurational entropy. This approximation neglects the short-range order that develops on cooling. In this study, we show that the conventional approximation is the first term of an infinite expansion of the free energy in energy cumulants. Higher-order cumulants are estimated from energies of random arrangements, without Monte Carlo or molecular dynamics. In a nine-element refractory system, adding the second cumulant reduced free energy errors by about an order of magnitude. The expansion gives phase diagrams with order--disorder transitions, defect concentrations, and short-range order. To demonstrate its utility, we used a foundation interatomic potential to screen lithium-excess rocksalt oxides across 26 elements for synthesizable disordered phases rich in the Li$_4$ clusters needed for lithium percolation. The approach applies to any lattice and chemistry, and brings disordered phases within reach of routine screening.

title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
abstract: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. The contribution is an architecture that separates engineering state, deterministic reasoning, grounded language realization, verification, and human release.

title: Tunable Ultrastrong Magnon-Magnon Coupling and Squeezed States in a Triaxial Van der Waals Antiferromagnet
abstract: Achieving and quantifying ultrastrong magnon-magnon coupling (USC) remains a key challenge for quantum magnonics. Here, we demonstrate widely tunable USC between chiral (right- and left-handed) and acoustic or optical magnon modes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet $CrPS_4$. Using a full quantum model, we decompose the interaction into three microscopic interaction channels: the co-rotating term $g_1$ (mode hybridization), the counter-rotating term $g_2$ (two-mode squeezing), and, uniquely in the chiral regime, the self-squared term $g_3$ that mediates single-mode squeezing. The normalized coupling ratio reaches $g/f_g$ $\sim$ 0.41, entering the USC regime. Most significantly, we establish a complete protocol linking these USC parameters to a measurable quantum phenomenon: a squeezed magnon vacuum state. Our simulations not only visualize the chirality and polarization evolution of the hybrid modes but also demonstrate how to directly extract quadrature fluctuations and a substantial squeezing factor (up to $\sim$ 9.7 dB) from thermal noise-driven magnetization dynamics. This work provides a material-specific quantum framework for USC and a practical pathway to detect and exploit non-classical magnon states in low-damping two-dimensional magnets, opening a route toward quantum-enhanced spintronics and hybrid quantum information platforms.

title: Benchmarking Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Temperature-Dependent Elasticity of Binary and High-Entropy Refractory Carbides
abstract: Accurate prediction of temperature-dependent elasticity is important for assessing refractory carbides under high-temperature conditions, but the computational cost of ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) limits systematic investigations across compositions and temperatures. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) offer an efficient alternative, yet their accuracy for this task remains insufficiently established. Here, we benchmark nine uMLIPs against consistent AIMD reference data for five binary and two high-entropy (HE) carbides between 300 and 1200 K. Elastic constants and the corresponding bulk, shear, and Young's moduli are obtained using stress-strain molecular dynamics, explicitly sampling thermal atomic motion and anharmonic effects beyond thermal expansion alone. We assess absolute elastic properties and normalized thermal softening separately. MACE-MH-1 achieves the lowest overall mean absolute percentage error (5.7%). MACE-MH-1 and DPA4-Mini reproduce thermal softening most accurately, with mean deviations of 2.5 and 2.3 percentage points, respectively. All models generally underestimate stiffness, with larger equilibrium volumes relative to the AIMD reference likely contributing to this trend for most models. C12 exhibits the largest model-dependent errors. The HE carbides are described with accuracy comparable to that of the binary carbides, indicating no apparent accuracy penalty from chemical complexity. Accuracy instead varies with transition-metal composition, with group-V carbides, particularly TaC, presenting the greatest challenge. These results identify promising pretrained models for finite-temperature elasticity in carbides and show why accurate absolute stiffness and thermal softening must be assessed independently.

title: Photoinduced Odd- and Mixed-Parity Magnetism in Collinear Antiferromagnets
abstract: Altermagnetism, characterized by compensated collinear magnetic moments and even-parity momentum-dependent spin splitting, has emerged as a distinct form of magnetic order. However, realizing odd- and mixed-parity magnetism in fully compensated collinear magnets remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate light-induced odd- and mixed-parity magnetism in conventional collinear antiferromagnets. Combining Floquet theory with first-principles calculations, we show that circularly polarized light (CPL) induces odd-parity $f$-wave spin splitting in monolayer CoS and CoSe, whereas elliptically polarized light (EPL) induces $p$-wave spin splitting. Uniaxial strain combined with CPL offers an alternative route to the $p$-wave state. Furthermore, combining an electric field with CPL or EPL generates mixed-parity spin splitting. Light-induced breaking of $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, together with spin-orbit coupling, gives rise to a finite anomalous Hall response. Our findings establish a versatile approach to engineering spin splitting and controlling electronic and magnetic properties in compensated antiferromagnets.

title: Magnon band splitting without altermagnetism in CuF2
abstract: Conclusive identification of an altermagnetic state requires going beyond mere symmetry arguments. We illustrate this in a combined computational and experimental study of the rutile-like material CuF$_2$, which is on the list of predicted altermagnets.
